_about: Hand-built estimate of Alaska's current account for calendar 2024, in billions of dollars. Each line has a central value, a low-high range, a confidence grade, how it was estimated and its source. scripts/build_pages.py adds the lines up, works out the goods-and-services balance from GDP minus spending by Alaskans, and combines the ranges. Edit a number here and rebuild; the page and the front-page panel follow.

absorption._about: Goods-and-services balance = GDP minus what Alaskans spend in Alaska and outside it (household consumption, private investment, state and local government). Federal spending in Alaska is treated as a sale to the outside, so it is not included here.

pce.label: Household consumption (PCE)
pce.basis: BEA personal consumption expenditures by state of residence, 2024. Includes what Alaskans spend while traveling outside.

investment.label: Private investment
investment.basis: Oil and gas capital spending of about $5B (DOR allowable lease expenditures: $7.5B in FY2024 and $8.6B forecast for FY2025, less about $2.9B of operating costs), plus about $2B of other private construction (AGC 2024 forecast, excluding oil and gas), about $2B of business equipment and vehicles, and $0.4B of mine capital spending.
investment.source: DOR Revenue Sources Book; AGC Alaska Construction Spending Forecast 2024

state_local.label: State and local government spending
state_local.basis: Wages, purchases and construction by state and local governments, excluding Medicaid payments (already in household consumption), the dividend and other cash transfers. Built from government's $13.2B share of GDP less the federal portion, plus purchases and public construction.
state_local.source: BEA GDP by state; AGC 2024 forecast

lines.label: Crude oil
lines.basis: North Slope output of about 464,500 barrels a day (average of FY2024 and FY2025) times an ANS West Coast price of about $80 (average of FY2024's $85.24 and FY2025's $74.48), for 366 days. Valued at the delivered price; tanker shipping is on the import side.
lines.source: DOR Revenue Sources Book, Fall 2024 and Spring 2025

lines.label: Metals (zinc, gold, silver, lead)
lines.basis: Value of metal produced by Alaska mines in 2024. USGS puts all nonfuel minerals at $4.7B, but sand, gravel and rock are used in the state.
lines.source: DGGS, Alaska's Mineral Industry; USGS via DGGS

lines.label: Seafood
lines.basis: First wholesale value in 2024. Nearly all of it is sold outside Alaska. Includes fish processed at sea by Seattle-based catcher-processors, which BEA does not count in Alaska's GDP; see the notes.
lines.source: McKinley Research Group for ASMI, Economic Value of Alaska's Seafood Industry (2026)

lines.label: Visitor spending
lines.basis: Direct spending by out-of-state visitors in Alaska, May 2023 to April 2024. Excludes cruise fares and airfare paid outside.
lines.source: McKinley Research Group for ATIA

lines.label: Fuel and services for transiting air cargo
lines.basis: Rough estimate of jet fuel, landing fees, handling, crew lodging and maintenance bought at Anchorage by carriers flying between Asia and North America. Most of the fuel is itself shipped in, so much of this value reappears as imports.
lines.source: Estimate; AIAS annual reports; ANC economic impact studies

lines.label: Other goods and services
lines.basis: Placeholder for timber, refined products, and business services sold outside, including spending in Alaska by nonresident workers that is not otherwise counted.
lines.source: Estimate

lines.label: Federal purchases from Alaska businesses
lines.basis: Federal contracts performed in Alaska, much of it Defense Department construction, utilities and supplies. Treated as an export of goods and services to the federal government.
lines.source: ISER analysis presented at Commonwealth North, 2026; USAspending

lines.label: Federal civilian and military payroll
lines.basis: Wages the federal government pays in Alaska. Civilian wages alone were $1.54B in federal FY2024; the rest is military pay. Treated as an export of government services, because the employer is outside the state.
lines.source: ISER (Commonwealth North, 2026); DOLWD Alaska Economic Trends, May 2025

lines.label: Permanent Fund cash income
lines.basis: Interest, dividends and real estate income of the Permanent Fund: $1.66B in FY2024 and $2.00B in FY2025, averaged for calendar 2024. Capital gains are excluded, as in national accounts; see the Permanent Fund section.
lines.source: APFC 2025 Annual Report

lines.label: Other state investment income
lines.basis: Interest and dividends on other state savings managed by Treasury (Constitutional Budget Reserve, endowments, operating funds), about $10B at roughly 4%. State pension funds are counted in the household line through BEA.
lines.source: Estimate

lines.label: Household and pension investment income from outside
lines.basis: BEA counts $10.8B of dividends, interest and rent received by Alaskans in 2024, including income credited through pension funds. About 70% (range 60 to 80%) is assumed to come from outside the state, after removing rent and interest paid within Alaska.
lines.source: BEA via FRED, AKODIV; share is an estimate

lines.label: Earnings of Alaska-owned firms outside Alaska
lines.basis: Profits that Alaska-headquartered companies, mainly Alaska Native regional and village corporations, earn on contracts and businesses outside the state. ASRC alone had $5.7B of revenue in 2024.
lines.source: Estimate; Alaska Business Top 49ers and ANCSA corporation reports

lines.label: Wages earned by nonresident workers
lines.basis: Nonresidents held almost 23% of non-federal jobs in 2024 and earned about $3.8B, about 17% of non-federal wages.
lines.source: DOLWD, Nonresidents Working in Alaska 2024

lines.label: Earnings of nonresident fishermen
lines.basis: Nonresidents took 57% of gross harvesting earnings; ex-vessel value was $1.3B in 2024, so about $0.74B gross. About 60% is taken as net income after fuel, gear and other costs bought in Alaska.
lines.source: DOLWD, Nonresidents Working in Alaska 2024; ASMI (2026)

lines.label: Oil producers' profits
lines.basis: Profit after state taxes and royalties and before federal income tax, on North Slope production owned almost entirely outside Alaska. Two methods: DOR's FY2024 barrel economics (wellhead value less operating cost, state and local taxes, royalties and depreciation) give about $2.9B; scaling ConocoPhillips' 2024 Alaska results to the whole slope, with a discount for fields still in development, gives about $3.5B.
lines.source: DOR Revenue Sources Book; ConocoPhillips 2024 10-K and Alaska earnings release

lines.label: Mine owners' profits
lines.basis: About a 30% operating margin on $4.0B of metal at 2024 prices, less royalties paid to NANA (Alaska-owned) and state mining taxes. The large mines are owned by companies in Canada, Australia, Idaho and Illinois.
lines.source: Estimate; DGGS

lines.label: Other out-of-state owners' profits
lines.basis: Profits of out-of-state retailers, banks, telecoms, oilfield service firms, tour operators, hospital systems and others on their Alaska business.
lines.source: Estimate

lines.label: Interest paid to outside lenders
lines.basis: Interest on Alaska mortgages, most of which are sold to national investors, plus consumer loans from out-of-state lenders and state and municipal bonds held outside Alaska.
lines.source: Estimate

lines.label: Federal benefits paid to Alaskans
lines.basis: Social Security, Medicare, veterans' benefits, SNAP, SSI, refundable tax credits and federal retirement. BEA's federally funded transfers to Alaskans add up to about $6.4B in 2024.
lines.source: ISER (Commonwealth North, 2026); BEA SAINC35 via ArcticStat

lines.label: Federal grants to governments, tribes and nonprofits
lines.basis: Includes the federal share of Medicaid, highway and broadband money, and grants to tribes and tribal health organizations. The state alone received $6.1B of federal receipts in FY2024; ISER puts grants at about $4B. The middle of the range is used.
lines.source: DOR Revenue Sources Book, Fall 2024; ISER (Commonwealth North, 2026)

lines.label: Federal taxes paid by Alaskans
lines.basis: IRS gross collections from Alaska filers were $6.74B in federal FY2023 and $7.90B in FY2025, when $0.88B was refunded. About $6.6B net for 2024, plus about $0.2B of federal excise taxes not credited to states.
lines.source: IRS Data Book, Table 5

lines.label: Private transfers out
lines.basis: Money sent abroad by Alaska residents and donations to organizations outside the state, net of gifts coming in.
lines.source: Estimate

apf_realized_gains.basis: Permanent Fund realized gains for calendar 2024, approximated as statutory net income less cash income: $2.54B in FY2024 and $3.87B in FY2025.
